scenarios.label: Broker-originated home loan
scenarios.rationale: The dominant path, but the mix differs sharply by bank.
scenarios.note: Responsible lending under the National Credit Code applies; business-purpose lending is exempt.

scenarios.label: Digital opening, KYC and ConnectID
scenarios.rationale: Identity now increasingly verified through ConnectID, the bank-owned digital identity exchange enabled by all four majors in January 2025.
scenarios.note: Corrected: FCS Coverage and CDR Scope Status are now explicit classes on every deposit account.

scenarios.label: Property settlement through PEXA
scenarios.rationale: Loan funding, title transfer and duty complete together on a platform the bank doesn't own.
scenarios.note: Duty Authority is the state revenue office; title identifiers are state-specific.

scenarios.label: Guarantor and family pledge
scenarios.rationale: A third party's property secures another party's loan.
scenarios.note: Code Part B6 sets disclosure and cooling-off obligations before a guarantee is taken.

scenarios.label: Guarantor enforcement
scenarios.rationale: What happens when the bank actually calls on the guarantee — the scenario nobody models until it happens.
scenarios.note: New scenario. Code B6 protections and AFCA determinations both bite here.

scenarios.label: SMSF limited recourse borrowing
scenarios.rationale: WITHDRAWN. All majors exited; new residential LRBAs banned from 10 August 2026.
scenarios.note: Back-book only. Business real property LRBAs remain permitted; existing arrangements grandfathered.

scenarios.label: Housing Australia 5% Deposit Scheme
scenarios.rationale: The Commonwealth guarantees up to 15% of value, displacing LMI.
scenarios.note: Administered through a panel of participating lenders including all four majors.

scenarios.label: Construction progressive drawdown
scenarios.rationale: One facility, many drawdowns, repeated valuations against stages of works.
scenarios.note: Confirm which of the six write construction loans.

scenarios.label: Offset and redraw
scenarios.rationale: Offset is a separate at-call deposit account; redraw is a feature of the loan. Offset balances do not reduce principal.
scenarios.note: Offset Link is now its own class — offsets are many-to-one against splits, not a field on the loan.

applicability.note: Up to 10 — but ubank is offset-limited.
Multiple Everyday Offset accounts — but Unloan has none.
Up to 10 offsets per variable loan.

scenarios.label: Split loan and package restructure
scenarios.rationale: One facility, several sub-accounts, bundled under a package with one annual fee.
scenarios.note: Several banks have retired package products — verify before treating as universal.

scenarios.label: Term deposit maturity and rollover
scenarios.rationale: A dated agreement that expires and either rolls or returns funds.
scenarios.note: 31-day term deposits are basic banking products but still within DDO per RG 274.

scenarios.label: Cash management account as adviser hub
scenarios.rationale: The settlement account sitting inside wrap and SMSF structures. Distinctively Macquarie.
scenarios.note: New scenario. A CMA is not an ordinary savings account — it has adviser authority attached.

applicability.note: The Macquarie CMA is widely used as the adviser/SMSF settlement hub.

scenarios.label: Statutory trust and controlled money accounts
scenarios.rationale: Solicitors', conveyancers' and real estate agents' trust accounts — governed by state legislation, not banking law.
scenarios.note: New scenario. Tranche 2 brings the professions themselves into the AML regime from 1 July 2026.

scenarios.label: PayTo mandate setup
scenarios.rationale: Mandates live in the NPP Mandate Management Service with defined fields including initiator ABN/ACN.
scenarios.note: Corrected: AusPayNet withdrew the June 2030 BECS end-date in December 2025. Do not hard-code a retirement date.

scenarios.label: Cheque wind-down migration
scenarios.rationale: No issuance after 30 June 2028; no acceptance after 30 September 2029; system closure by 2030.
scenarios.note: New scenario. AusPayNet holds ACCC authorisation for the Cheques Transition Program from 24 July 2025.

scenarios.label: Mistaken internet payment recovery
scenarios.rationale: Money sent to the wrong account. The ePayments Code sets the recovery process between banks.
scenarios.note: New scenario. Confirmation of Payee is being rolled out to reduce these at source.

scenarios.label: Joint account and separation
scenarios.rationale: The operating rule belongs to the arrangement, not either person.
scenarios.note: FCS splits joint balances equally between holders for the $250,000 per-holder cap.

scenarios.label: Power of attorney and loss of capacity
scenarios.rationale: Delegated authority needs an effective date and a scope.
scenarios.note: Enduring versus general matters a great deal.

scenarios.label: Deceased estate
scenarios.rationale: The customer persists as a Party but can no longer act.
scenarios.note: Code Part B8 sets timeframes for deceased estate handling.

scenarios.label: First Nations and vulnerable customer access
scenarios.rationale: Standard identity documents and fixed addresses cannot be assumed.
scenarios.note: Code B3 covers basic and low-fee accounts for concession-card holders.

scenarios.label: Unclaimed monies and the Financial Claims Scheme
scenarios.rationale: Dormant accounts transfer to ASIC; the FCS guarantees deposits to $250,000 per holder per ADI.
scenarios.note: FCS aggregates per ADI, not per brand — Westpac and St.George share one cap.

scenarios.label: Financial hardship
scenarios.rationale: Statutory clocks start on notice. What is decided follows the customer for years.
scenarios.note: Financial Hardship Information distinguishes temporary FHA from variation FHA.
regulatoryReferences: Privacy Act Part IIIA / CR Code

scenarios.label: Arrears through to default
scenarios.rationale: The process is regulated, not just the outcome.
scenarios.note: A hardship notice arriving mid-path stops this cold.

scenarios.label: Farm debt mediation before enforcement
scenarios.rationale: Mandatory mediation before a bank can enforce against a farm mortgage. State-based, not federal.
scenarios.note: New scenario. Reinforced by Code Part B7 (farmers).

applicability.note: Farmland sits in Macquarie Asset Management, not the bank.

scenarios.label: Complaint escalating to AFCA
scenarios.rationale: RG 271 mandates a line-item complaint dataset reported to ASIC, not a summary count.
scenarios.note: Merge candidate with scam and chargeback — all feed the same IDR dataset.

scenarios.label: Sanctions and PEP screening
scenarios.rationale: Screening attaches to the Party, before and throughout the relationship.
scenarios.note: The restructured AML/CTF regime commences 31 March 2026.

scenarios.label: AML alert through to SMR
scenarios.rationale: Evidence is the relationship path, not any single record.
scenarios.note: Every lending, deposit, FX and custody service is independently a designated service under s6.

scenarios.label: Scam and reimbursement under the SPF
scenarios.rationale: The customer authorised it. Civil penalties reach $50 million per contravention.
scenarios.note: Corrected: Act commenced 21 February 2025; draft rules ~September 2026; bank sector code obligations from ~2027.

scenarios.label: Card dispute and chargeback
scenarios.rationale: Scheme rules dictate the lifecycle of a dispute on a transaction the bank owns.
scenarios.note: For ING and Macquarie the merchant leg sits outside the bank.

scenarios.label: International payment and IFTI
scenarios.rationale: Every cross-border transfer of any value generates a report.
scenarios.note: Migrating to the IFTI-E v2.0 schema under AUSTRAC's REST program.

scenarios.label: Merchant acquiring and settlement
scenarios.rationale: An organisation as customer, settlement counterparty and borrower at once.
scenarios.note: Corrected to Not Applicable for ING and Macquarie.

applicability.note: No business transaction account, so no acquiring.
Own help centre states it does not offer this service.

scenarios.label: Least-cost routing and the surcharge ban
scenarios.rationale: From 1 October 2026 surcharging is removed on eftpos, Mastercard and Visa debit, prepaid and credit; debit interchange caps fall to 0.16% or 8c and consumer credit to 0.3%.
scenarios.note: New scenario. The RBA estimates the interchange cuts lower merchant wholesale costs by ~$910m a year. Foreign-card cap 1.0% from 1 April 2027.

scenarios.label: BNPL instalment plan
scenarios.rationale: CommBank StepPay and NAB Now Pay Later. BNPL is being brought inside the National Credit Code as a low cost credit contract.
scenarios.note: New scenario. Reclassification means DDO, responsible lending and credit reporting now attach.
regulatoryReferences: National Credit Code (low cost credit contract)

applicability.note: StepPay: $100-$2,000 split into four fortnightly instalments on Mastercard rails.

scenarios.label: Equipment finance and chattel mortgage
scenarios.rationale: Security over personal property, not land — so it registers on the PPSR, not a titles office.
scenarios.note: New scenario. PPSR Registration is now a class — priority disputes turn on registration timing.

scenarios.label: Invoice finance and PPSR priority
scenarios.rationale: Lending against a receivables ledger, where priority against other secured creditors is everything.
scenarios.note: New scenario. The ledger is a moving population, not a fixed asset.

scenarios.label: Novated lease
scenarios.rationale: A three-party arrangement between employee, employer and financier — the employer pays but the employee owns the obligation.
scenarios.note: New scenario. Confirm current provision at each bank.

scenarios.label: Agribusiness seasonal facility
scenarios.rationale: Cash arrives twice a year. Farm Management Deposits are an Australia-only tax-structured product.
scenarios.note: Corrected to Not Applicable for ING and Macquarie.

applicability.note: Describes itself as Australia's leading agribusiness bank.

scenarios.label: Business lending and beneficial ownership
scenarios.rationale: The borrower is an organisation, but the people behind it must be identified.
scenarios.note: The Code's small business threshold rose from $3m to $5m in aggregate borrowings, bringing in ~10,000 more businesses.

scenarios.label: Family trust banking
scenarios.rationale: The account belongs to the trust; the trustee operates it.
scenarios.note: If Party can only be a person or a company, this fails.

scenarios.label: Letter of credit lifecycle
scenarios.rationale: Issuance, presentation, discrepancy, payment — a document-driven contract with its own event chain.
scenarios.note: New scenario. Discrepant documents are the norm, not the exception — model the discrepancy state.

scenarios.label: Bank guarantee issuance
scenarios.rationale: A contingent liability, not a loan — commonly used for commercial lease bonds and construction retentions.
scenarios.note: New scenario. Off-balance-sheet exposure with its own capital treatment.

scenarios.label: Documentary collection
scenarios.rationale: The bank handles documents but takes no credit risk — a different obligation shape from an LC.
scenarios.note: New scenario. Frequently confused with an LC in data models; the risk position is opposite.

scenarios.label: Derivative trade under an ISDA
scenarios.rationale: The master agreement, not the trade, is the contract. Trades are confirmations under it.
scenarios.note: New scenario. ISDA Master Agreement and CSA are now classes. Foreign-booked trades attract host-country regimes.

scenarios.label: Margin call and close-out netting
scenarios.rationale: Collateral moves daily under the CSA. On default, everything nets to a single figure.
scenarios.note: New scenario. Close-out netting is why the master agreement must be a first-class object.

scenarios.label: Repo and securities lending
scenarios.rationale: Secured funding against securities. Reported separately from lending in ARF 721.
scenarios.note: New scenario. GMRA is the repo analogue to ISDA.

scenarios.label: Custody and asset servicing
scenarios.rationale: Holding assets for someone else is independently a designated service under the AML Act.
scenarios.note: New scenario. ING does not offer custody.

scenarios.label: Commodity hedging
scenarios.rationale: Energy, agricultural and metals hedging for corporate clients. Distinctively Macquarie.
scenarios.note: New scenario. Physical commodity positions differ from financial derivatives in capital treatment.

applicability.note: Commodities & Global Markets is a defining Macquarie business.

scenarios.label: Share trading and CHESS holdings
scenarios.rationale: Securities held under a HIN are a different asset class with a different registry.
scenarios.note: Corrected with the ANZ divestment confirmed.

applicability.note: ANZ Share Investing closed 15 March 2023; ~500,000 clients and A$45bn+ transferred to CMC Markets.

scenarios.label: Margin lending
scenarios.rationale: Borrowing to invest, secured over the portfolio. Notably exempt from DDO.
scenarios.note: New scenario. Margin loans are one of the few products expressly excepted from the design and distribution obligations.

scenarios.label: Wrap platform and superannuation
scenarios.rationale: Most majors have exited manufacturing — CBA sold 55% of Colonial First State to KKR — so these are now largely distributed, not owned.
scenarios.note: New scenario. Model the issuer-versus-distributor distinction carefully — the licence may not be the bank's.

applicability.note: Macquarie Wrap is a core business.

scenarios.label: Insurance distribution
scenarios.rationale: After the wealth divestments the banks distribute under someone else's licence. Add-on insurance carries a deferred sales model.
scenarios.note: New scenario. Issuer versus distributor is now an explicit role pair — the obligation set differs.

scenarios.label: Securitisation and covered bonds
scenarios.rationale: The mortgage pool leaves the balance sheet, or is ring-fenced. Either way the loans keep serving.
scenarios.note: New scenario. The customer relationship is unchanged; the ownership and capital treatment are not.

scenarios.label: Brand migration after acquisition
scenarios.rationale: ANZ completed the Suncorp acquisition on 31 July 2024 and plans to migrate customers to ANZ Plus by ~September 2027, returning the Norfina licence.
scenarios.note: New scenario. Returning a licence collapses two deposit guarantees into one — a real customer impact.

applicability.note: Norfina Limited is presently a separate ADI, so its FCS cap is currently distinct.
Citi consumer business completed 1 June 2022; white-label card book retained.

scenarios.label: White-label and referral distribution
scenarios.rationale: The customer sees one brand, the funder is another, the servicer may be a third.
scenarios.note: New scenario. DDO makes the distributor separately liable — so the role must be modelled, not implied.

applicability.note: Advantedge wholesale mortgages; the acquired Citi book issues cards for Coles, Qantas, Virgin Money, Kogan and others.

scenarios.label: CDR consent and data sharing
scenarios.rationale: Scope narrowed from 4 March 2025 — sharing became voluntary for certain covered products, and only standard consumer vehicle loans are mandatory in asset finance.
scenarios.note: Corrected: CDR Scope Status is now an explicit per-product enum — mandatory, voluntary or out of scope.

scenarios.label: APRA economic and financial statistics
scenarios.rationale: Every product maps to a form, and every form demands dimensions captured at origination.
scenarios.note: Corrected: dimensions are resident/non-resident, borrower type and sector, ANZSIC 2006, loan purpose, product type, security type and interest-rate type. Credit reported gross of offset and redraw.

scenarios.label: Capital and prudential reporting
scenarios.rationale: Each product attracts a different standard and a different risk weight. IRB banks and standardised banks compute differently.
scenarios.note: New scenario. The majors and Macquarie are IRB-accredited; the treatment differs from standardised.

scenarios.label: Financial accountability regime
scenarios.rationale: Commenced for ADIs and their NOHCs on 15 March 2024, replacing BEAR. Accountable persons map to product lines.
scenarios.note: A legal fact about a person, not an org-chart box.

scenarios.label: Design and distribution breach
scenarios.rationale: Basic banking products are within DDO; margin loans and MySuper are excepted.
scenarios.note: Corrected: distributors must notify the issuer of significant dealings within 10 business days; issuers notify ASIC within 10.

scenarios.label: Credit reporting and repayment history
scenarios.rationale: The bank supplies monthly and consumes at assessment. Errors flow both ways.
scenarios.note: BNPL reclassification brings instalment plans into this pipeline.

scenarios.label: CPS 230 — a critical service goes down
scenarios.rationale: Consolidates the former CPS 231 and CPS 232. Registers were due 1 October 2025; pre-existing contracts covered by 1 July 2026.
scenarios.note: The bank must understand its suppliers' suppliers.

scenarios.label: Branch closure and channel shift
scenarios.rationale: The counter and the ATM your customer uses are often not your assets.
scenarios.note: Suncorp retains its own separate Bank@Post agreement.

applicability.note: Launched Bank@Post 17 December 2025 across 3,300+ Post Offices.

scenarios.label: Foreign parent and offshore booking
scenarios.rationale: ING Bank (Australia) sits under ING Groep, ECB-supervised at group level. NAB has BNZ and CBA has ASB, both RBNZ-regulated. Institutional trades booked offshore attract host regimes.
scenarios.note: New scenario. The licence hierarchy — NOHC, ADI, Brand — is now explicit in the model.

applicability.note: Norfina is a separate ADI pending licence return.
Wholly owned by ING Groep N.V.

scenarios.label: Refinance, discharge and security substitution
scenarios.rationale: How loans end. Also covers portability — swapping the security without discharging the loan.
scenarios.note: Restored after audit. Discharge Authority and Account Closure are both distinct from the loan itself.

scenarios.label: IDR complaint data reporting to ASIC
scenarios.rationale: A line-item complaint dataset reported to ASIC, not a summary count. Restored as its own trace.
scenarios.note: Restored after audit. The reporting obligation is separate from resolving the complaint.

scenarios.label: Fees, interest accrual and statements
scenarios.rationale: The everyday machinery. Balances are a projection over these events, never a stored fact.
scenarios.note: Added after audit. Fee income by product is separately reportable.

scenarios.label: Dishonour and returned payment
scenarios.rationale: A payment that fails. Direct debits, PayTo mandates and scheduled payments each fail differently.
scenarios.note: Added after audit. The dishonour is the bridge between a missed payment and an arrears event.

scenarios.label: Product switch and variation
scenarios.rationale: Fixed to variable, package to basic, owner-occupier to investor. Each switch re-tests the target market.
scenarios.note: Added after audit. Changing loan purpose changes the EFS classification — a common reporting break.

scenarios.label: Account closure and dormancy
scenarios.rationale: Accounts end by request, by dormancy, or by death. Dormant balances eventually leave the bank entirely.
scenarios.note: Added after audit. Seven years of inactivity is the usual trigger — verify the current threshold.

scenarios.label: Remediation program
scenarios.rationale: Systemic error found, cohort identified, money returned. The scenario every royal commission produced.
scenarios.note: Added after audit. Remediation needs a cohort definition, which needs the product and time boundaries to be modelled.

scenarios.label: Line of credit, overdraft and bridging
scenarios.rationale: Revolving and interim credit. The limit, not the balance, is the exposure.
scenarios.note: Added after audit. Undrawn limits carry capital under APS 112 — the balance alone understates exposure.

scenarios.label: Reverse mortgage and equity release
scenarios.rationale: Interest capitalises, nothing is repaid until death or sale. Statutory no-negative-equity protection applies.
scenarios.note: Added after audit. Most majors exited; the Government's Home Equity Access Scheme now fills much of this space.

scenarios.label: PayID, Osko, BPAY and Confirmation of Payee
scenarios.rationale: Addressing and verification. PayID had over 25 million registrations by April 2025; Confirmation of Payee is rolling out to cut mis-payment and scams at source.
scenarios.note: Added after audit. PayID and Confirmation of Payee were both named in the research and missing from the model.

scenarios.label: Digital wallet and tokenised card
scenarios.rationale: The card in the wallet is a token, not the card. Provisioning is its own event with its own fraud surface.
scenarios.note: Added after audit. Mobile-wallet least-cost routing was deferred to an RBA consultation expected mid-2026.

scenarios.label: Payment gateway and payroll
scenarios.rationale: Business payment services beyond the terminal — online acceptance and outbound salary runs.
scenarios.note: Added after audit. Payroll is a bulk direct-entry flow — exposed to the BECS migration.

scenarios.label: Foreign currency account and travel card
scenarios.rationale: Balances held in a currency other than AUD. Note the FCS does not protect foreign-currency deposits.
scenarios.note: Added after audit. The FCS covers AUD-denominated deposits only — a real customer-disclosure point.

scenarios.label: Supply chain finance
scenarios.rationale: The bank pays a supplier early against a buyer's approved invoice. Whose exposure is it — buyer or supplier?
scenarios.note: Added after audit. Classification as buyer debt versus supplier finance drives the capital and disclosure treatment.

scenarios.label: Debt capital markets issuance
scenarios.rationale: Arranging and distributing a bond issue for a client, or for the bank's own funding.
scenarios.note: Added after audit. The bank is arranger, sometimes issuer, and sometimes investor — three roles, one deal.

scenarios.label: Structured product distribution
scenarios.rationale: A derivative wrapped as an investment. The TMD obligations bite hardest here.
scenarios.note: Added after audit. ASIC's product intervention powers have been used in this space.

scenarios.label: Private banking and family office
scenarios.rationale: High-net-worth relationships spanning lending, markets, custody and trusts under one coverage banker.
scenarios.note: Added after audit. Private clients are disproportionately PEPs and complex structures — enhanced CDD is the norm.

scenarios.label: Superannuation trustee obligations
scenarios.rationale: Where the bank still holds an RSE licence it is a trustee, not a product provider — a different duty entirely.
scenarios.note: Added after audit. Most majors have exited; model this only where the licence is retained.

scenarios.label: Safe deposit box
scenarios.rationale: The bank holds contents it never sees. On death or default, access becomes a legal problem.
scenarios.note: Added after audit. Branch closures are steadily retiring these — confirm current availability.

scenarios.label: Correspondent banking due diligence
scenarios.rationale: Banking another bank. Explicitly regulated as its own category because the bank cannot see the underlying customers.
scenarios.note: Added after audit. Nested correspondent relationships are the risk — you may be several banks removed from the payer.

scenarios.label: Add-on insurance and deferred sales
scenarios.rationale: Consumer credit insurance sold alongside a loan or card cannot be sold at the same moment. A mandatory pause applies.
scenarios.note: Added after audit. The deferred sales model was a direct royal commission outcome and applies to add-on products.

scenarios.label: Credit card origination and limit
scenarios.rationale: A revolving credit facility with a limit, accessed by a card. The limit is the exposure, not the balance.
scenarios.note: Undrawn card limits carry capital under APS 112 — the outstanding balance understates exposure.

applicability.note: Wound back credit card new business — confirm current position.

scenarios.label: Card issuance, expiry and reissue
scenarios.rationale: The card is a physical or virtual instrument distinct from the account it accesses. It is issued, activated, expires and is reissued on its own cycle.
scenarios.note: Three parties on one piece of plastic: primary cardholder, additional cardholder, and the account owner who is liable.

scenarios.label: Lost or stolen card and replacement
scenarios.rationale: Block, dispute, replace. The ePayments Code sets who bears the loss for unauthorised transactions.
scenarios.note: Tokenised wallet credentials survive a physical replacement — a common operational gap.

scenarios.label: Balance transfer, cash advance and minimum repayment
scenarios.rationale: Three different interest treatments on one account. Cash advances accrue immediately; balance transfers sit at a promotional rate; the minimum repayment governs how slowly the rest is repaid.
scenarios.note: Payment allocation order between balances is regulated under the National Credit Code.

scenarios.label: Credit limit increase and reduction
scenarios.rationale: Unsolicited credit limit increase offers are prohibited. Every increase needs express consent and a fresh assessment.
scenarios.note: Reductions can be unilateral; increases cannot. The asymmetry has to be in the model.

scenarios.label: Rewards accrual and redemption
scenarios.rationale: A points balance is a liability the bank owes the customer, sitting alongside the money it is owed.
scenarios.note: Points expiry, transfer to airline programs and co-brand partners all need modelling if loyalty is material.

scenarios.label: No-interest and low-fee cards
scenarios.rationale: CommBank Neo and NAB StraightUp charge a monthly fee rather than interest — a structurally different credit product.
scenarios.note: No interest does not mean no credit — responsible lending and DDO still apply.

scenarios.label: Card hardship and persistent debt
scenarios.rationale: Revolving debt that never clears. Card hardship behaves differently from a term loan because there is no fixed end date.
scenarios.note: Persistent minimum-repayment behaviour is a recognised harm indicator.

scenarios.label: Debit, prepaid and gift cards
scenarios.rationale: Debit cards are dual-network in Australia, which is what makes least-cost routing possible. Stored value and gift cards are a separate regulated instrument.
scenarios.note: Large debit issuers are expected to keep issuing dual-network cards; 84% of merchants were LCR-enabled by December 2025.

scenarios.label: Personal, car and green loans
scenarios.rationale: Fixed-term consumer credit. Car loans take security over the vehicle and register on the PPSR; unsecured personal loans do not.
scenarios.note: Green and EV loan discounts are a pricing feature, not a separate product class.

applicability.note: Wound back personal lending new business — confirm.

scenarios.label: Basic, youth and concession accounts
scenarios.rationale: The Banking Code requires basic and low-fee accounts for people with low or no income, and for concession card holders.
scenarios.note: RG 274 confirms basic banking products remain within the design and distribution obligations.
regulatoryReferences: DDO / TMD (basic banking products in scope)

scenarios.label: Complimentary card travel insurance claim
scenarios.rationale: Free cover attached to a platinum or signature card — but only if activated, and only if enough of the trip was paid on the card.
scenarios.note: Three parties before a claim is even lodged: underwriter, agent, and the bank as distributor earning commission.

applicability.note: Underwritten by Zurich, issued and managed by agent Cover-More; requires activation and a $500 prepaid travel spend.

scenarios.label: LMI claim on mortgagee sale
scenarios.rationale: The insured party is the lender. The borrower pays the premium and may still be pursued for the shortfall afterwards.
scenarios.note: The asymmetry between who pays and who is covered is the most misunderstood relationship in mortgage lending.

scenarios.label: Scheme guarantee displacing LMI
scenarios.rationale: The Commonwealth guarantee substitutes for LMI entirely. Same risk position, different counterparty, no premium.
scenarios.note: CBA signalled in March 2025 it was unlikely to renew its Helia contract — scheme substitution is reshaping the LMI market.

scenarios.label: Consumer credit insurance and deferred sales
scenarios.rationale: Sold alongside a loan or card, and the source of some of the largest remediation programs in Australian banking.
scenarios.note: The deferred sales model commenced 5 October 2021 as a direct royal commission outcome.

scenarios.label: Life and risk insurance referral
scenarios.rationale: After the divestments the banks refer, they do not underwrite. TAL holds the ex-Westpac book, AIA the ex-CommInsure book, Zurich the ex-ANZ book.
scenarios.note: The bank's obligation is distribution and referral conduct — the prudential risk sits with the insurer.

applicability.note: CommInsure sold to AIA with a 20-year bancassurance arrangement.

scenarios.label: General insurance distribution
scenarios.rationale: Home, contents, motor, landlord and strata — distributed under a third-party underwriter's licence.
scenarios.note: The Financial Claims Scheme covers general insurer failure separately from the $250,000 deposit cap.

scenarios.label: Claims handling as a financial service
scenarios.rationale: Since 1 January 2022 handling and settling a claim is itself a licensed financial service, not back-office administration.
scenarios.note: A Hayne recommendation. It converts claims denial into a licensed-conduct question.

scenarios.label: Three-party scheme settlement
scenarios.rationale: American Express and Diners Club are issuer, acquirer and scheme at once. No big-four bank issues Amex companion cards any longer.
scenarios.note: Marked N for all six: companion card issuance has ceased. Retained to explain why the four-party split does not apply here.

scenarios.label: Four-party scheme and interchange
scenarios.rationale: Issuer, acquirer, scheme and merchant. Interchange flows from acquirer to issuer, and the RBA caps it.
scenarios.note: From 1 October 2026 debit interchange falls to 8c or 0.16% and consumer credit to 0.3%; a 1.0% foreign-issued card cap starts 1 April 2027.

scenarios.label: Dual-network routing choice
scenarios.rationale: One card, two networks. The merchant picks the cheaper rail — roughly 20% lower debit acceptance cost.
scenarios.note: 84% of merchants had in-person LCR enabled by end 2025; online and mobile-wallet routing remain the open questions for the RBA's mid-2026 consultation.

scenarios.label: White-label card issuance
scenarios.rationale: A Coles Mastercard is issued by NAB, branded Coles, on the Mastercard scheme. Three different organisations, one card.
scenarios.note: Issuer, brand and scheme diverge. A model that assumes they are the same organisation cannot represent this.

applicability.note: Holds the Citi-originated book issuing for Coles, Qantas, Virgin Money, BOQ, Kogan and others — predominantly Mastercard, while NAB's own-brand cards are Visa.

scenarios.label: Structured deposit distribution
scenarios.rationale: A deposit with a derivative return. It straddles two regulatory treatments and its FCS status depends on structure.
scenarios.note: Whether the FCS applies turns on whether the principal is a protected deposit.

scenarios.label: Credit bureau reporting and disputes
scenarios.rationale: Three bureaux, different scores, different lender preferences. Errors flow both ways and the correction path is regulated.
scenarios.note: Equifax is the majors' usual bureau for home loans; illion and Experian are used more by fintech and BNPL.

scenarios.label: ELNO choice and interoperability
scenarios.rationale: PEXA holds close to the whole market. Sympli is the competitor and ARNECC suspended the interoperability program in 2026.
scenarios.note: A near-monopoly on settlement is a concentration risk under CPS 230, not just a commercial fact.

scenarios.label: Aggregator accreditation and commission
scenarios.rationale: The bank accredits the aggregator, the aggregator accredits the broker, and commission flows back down the same chain.
scenarios.note: Best interests duty commenced 1 January 2021 under Part 3-5A of the NCCP Act.

applicability.note: Sold PLAN, Choice and FAST to Loan Market Group in 2021; those brands were retired into LMG in 2023. Advantedge stopped new applications 30 September 2025.

scenarios.label: Points accrual, caps and exclusions
scenarios.rationale: Every program caps the full earn rate and excludes whole categories. The exclusions are where customers get surprised.
scenarios.note: Government and ATO payments, BPAY, gambling, cash advances, fees, refunds and balance transfers are the standard exclusion set.

applicability.note: Altitude: full rate to $10,000 per statement period, then 0.5 pts/$1.
Ultimate Awards: bonus categories capped at $10,000 per period.
Rewards wound back; Qantas earning ended October 2024.

scenarios.label: Transfer to an airline or coalition partner
scenarios.rationale: No flexible bank program transfers directly to Qantas. Qantas requires a dedicated card variant with its own annual program fee.
scenarios.note: Westpac and St.George run periodic 15% bonus transfer windows to Velocity in May and November — the bonus window is a dated object, not a rate.

applicability.note: Altitude transfers 3:1 to Velocity, KrisFlyer, Asia Miles and Airpoints; 3:2 to Everyday Rewards. No direct Qantas.
NAB Rewards transfers 2:1 to Velocity, 3:1 to KrisFlyer and Asia Miles, plus Flybuys.

scenarios.label: Direct-earn airline card
scenarios.rationale: A paid overlay on the card. The points are the airline's liability, not the bank's — which is why most banks disclose no points liability.
scenarios.note: The bank buys points from the airline. The customer relationship for redemption sits with the airline.

applicability.note: Altitude Qantas, $75 annual Rewards Program Fee.
ANZ Frequent Flyer Black, 1 Qantas pt/$1 to $7,500 per period.

scenarios.label: Points expiry and forfeiture
scenarios.rationale: Points die three ways: a fixed clock, account inactivity, or closure. Forfeiture on closure is the one that generates complaints.
scenarios.note: The ACCC recommended prominent expiry alerts — in the subject line of an email, not buried in terms.

applicability.note: No expiry while active; 90 days to redeem on closure.
Points expire 36 months after the end of the year earned.
Points forfeited on closure or program switch.

scenarios.label: Sign-up bonus with minimum spend
scenarios.rationale: The headline number is conditional on spend within a window, and usually excluded if you held a similar card recently.
scenarios.note: High-rate rewards cards sold on bonus points are exactly what ASIC's credit card DDO surveillance targets.

applicability.note: Bonus eligibility excludes anyone who held an ANZ Frequent Flyer or Rewards card in the last 24 months.

scenarios.label: Merchant-funded cashback offer
scenarios.rationale: The retailer funds the discount and pays for targeted placement. The bank or the network holds the transaction data that does the targeting.
scenarios.note: This is where privacy and CDR obligations bite hardest — the offer is built from the customer's transaction history.

applicability.note: Westpac Extras, fulfilled via Mastercard or merchant partners, plus a separate ShopBack lounge.
Cashrewards was shut down in September 2025.
NAB Goodies runs on Visa; the technology vendor is undisclosed.
Yello Cashback Offers are powered by Mastercard, and CommBank collects personal information from Mastercard to target them.

scenarios.label: Tier status recognition
scenarios.rationale: Not a points program. A monthly review of relationship depth that unlocks cashback, discounts and early access.
scenarios.note: Marked applicable only to CBA. A relationship-tier model is structurally different from a points model and needs its own classes.

applicability.note: Yello has four tiers, reviewed monthly on the prior month's activity and held for three months once earned. Diamond gives $10/month cashback on Ultimate Awards. Extended to eligible sole traders and single-director companies.

scenarios.label: Tier benefit claim
scenarios.rationale: Lounge passes, concierge, purchase protection and rental excess cover all attach to the card tier. Several are insurance and are regulated as such.
scenarios.note: A complimentary benefit is still a financial product when it is insurance — DDO and claims handling both apply.
regulatoryReferences: ASIC (complimentary insurance is a financial product)

scenarios.label: Program devaluation and terms change
scenarios.rationale: Earn rates fall and redemption costs rise. Terms that allow unilateral change without notice are the ACCC's stated unfair-terms concern.
scenarios.note: The ACCC recommended clear prior notice or compensation before detrimental unilateral changes.

applicability.note: NAB Rewards terms allow the points required for redemption to change at any time without prior notice.
Cut earn rates and raised redemption cost on 1 July 2024.

scenarios.label: Points liability recognition
scenarios.rationale: Unredeemed points are deferred revenue. Whether the bank carries it depends on whether the points are its own currency or the airline's.
scenarios.note: Direct-earn cards push the liability to the airline. That is why only Westpac clearly discloses a figure.

applicability.note: Discloses credit card loyalty deferred income of $338 million at 30 September 2024, up from $324m in 2023.
No discrete points liability figure located.

scenarios.label: Coalition program linkage
scenarios.rationale: Supermarket coalition programs are the indirect route to Qantas, and the reason a grocery shop links to an airline balance.
scenarios.note: A weak indirect Qantas path, but the only one available from a flexible bank program.

applicability.note: Altitude transfers 3:2 to Everyday Rewards, which converts to Qantas 2:1.
NAB Rewards converts to Flybuys; Coles-branded cards issued by NAB earn Flybuys directly.

scenarios.label: Loyalty outside points
scenarios.rationale: Rate discounts, utility cashback and round-ups are loyalty mechanics attached to deposits and mortgages rather than cards.
scenarios.note: A rate discount is a loyalty benefit with credit-law consequences — it changes the contracted rate.

applicability.note: Unloan gives a loyalty rate discount that increases each year for up to 30 years.
1% cashback on eligible utility bills to $100 per financial year, plus Everyday Round Up into savings, a home loan or charity.

scenarios.label: Card controls and gambling blocks
scenarios.rationale: Customer-operated risk controls. The gambling block with a time-lock is a harm-minimisation feature, not a convenience.
scenarios.note: Confirmation of Payee under the Scam-Safe Accord; ANZ reports 140,000+ payments abandoned after mismatch alerts.

applicability.note: Gambling block carries a 48-hour time-lock; Digital Padlock kill switch live from August 2025.
Lock, block and limit controls per card.

scenarios.label: Property, identity and micro-investing services
scenarios.rationale: Non-banking services in the app that still carry regulatory weight — conveyancing, ID protection, and fractional investing.
scenarios.note: These sit outside the banking licence but inside the banking app — an increasingly common regulatory seam.

applicability.note: Home-in conveyancing, Truyu identity protection and Kit sit under x15ventures; CommSec Pocket covers micro-investing.
